newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kwoon Chung upside seen limited -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: Kwoon Chung upside seen limited -- analysts.

text.p: Shares in Kwoon Chung Bus Holdings Ltd are expected to go up on their trading debut on Wednesday, but analysts said the upside was limited for the Hong Kong-based bus line operator.

"We expect the shares to trade above the issue price judging from the grey market price and its encouraging flotation response," Sunny Chan, senior research manager from Seapower Research, said on Monday.
The grey market price of the shares was about HK$2.30 per shares, analysts said.

Kwoon Chung offered 59 million new shares at HK$1.80 per share, raising proceeds of HK$93 million to expand its bus related business in Hong Kong and China. The initial public offering was 53.5 times subscribed.
Dealing in the shares is expected to begin on September 25.

"We expect the shares to have a P/E (price earnings multiple) of about nine to 10 times, compared with its prospective P/E of 7.8 (at issue)," said Patrick Chia, research manager from China Everbright Securities.
Other listed companies in similar business had P/E's of 10 to 11, analysts noted.
But analysts generally said unexciting fundamentals would cap the upside.

"A valuation above 10 times P/E is not justified since its China projects are still at the planning stage and no solid contribution is seen in the immediate run," said a research manager at a regional brokerage.
"The concept of tapping the transportation business in China is attractive," said Chan. "However, investors are likely to take a more cautious stand in selecting them."
